metadata.note: The Nashua and Lowell Railroad (Lowell MA - Nashua NH, opened 1838, the first railroad in New Hampshire) and the three roads it worked: the Stony Brook RR (North Chelmsford - Ayer, 1848), the Wilton RR (Nashua - Wilton, opened in three legs 1848/1850/1851) and the Peterborough RR (Wilton - Greenfield, 1874). Operators over time (Rule 4): Nashua and Lowell 1838 - Feb 1857; a B&L/N&L pool under one management (manager George Stark of the N&L) Feb 1857 - Dec 1878; Nashua and Lowell alone Dec 1878 - Nov 1880; Boston and Lowell (100-year lease) 1880 - 1887; Boston and Maine (lease of the B&L) from 1887. Each line is drawn as one feature per operator sharing identical geometry. THE POOL IS NOT SPLIT: per the research report's recommended option (a), 1857-1878 stays inside the N&L features as its own segment, whose note describes the pool. Passenger ends: Lowell - Nashua 1967 (plus an MBTA-sponsored trial 1980-81), Stony Brook 1961, Nashua - Wilton 1936, Wilton - Greenfield last confirmed 1932 [OPEN]. A Wilton Scenic Railroad tourist operation ran Wilton - Greenfield 2003-2006. Freight after those years is context only (Rule 1). Lowell - Nashua was previously drawn inside the Concord/Northern feature in nh_concord_northern_railroads.geojson (1842-1967) and as a short N&L stub (1838-1842); both were moved here (see that file's nashua_lowell_fix). Not drawn, because the N&L did not run their trains: the Manchester & Keene beyond Greenfield, the Concord RR, the Worcester & Nashua, the Nashua & Rochester, the Nashua, Acton & Boston and the Fitchburg's Brookline & Milford line.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (schedules eff. 30 Sep 1951), cached at research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt
metadata.colours: Boston and Maine #1D3557 pulled from existing Boston and Maine Railroad features. New colours, none previously used by any company in data/: Nashua and Lowell #821458 (the N&L previously had no colour of its own - its 1838-1842 stub wore the B&M's), Boston and Lowell #429A28 (no Boston and Lowell company colour existed; its Lowell Line years are drawn in the MBTA's colour in mbta_commuter_rail.geojson, flagged for a Boston and Lowell pass), Wilton Scenic Railroad #E69E26.
not_yet_sourced: Wilton - Greenfield (Peterborough RR) B&M passenger end: [OPEN] at 1932, the last confirmed year (Fowler "c"); no source dates the actual end.

Nashua - Wilton: The Clio says one passenger car a day rode the freight 1936-1952 (a mixed train, which Rule 1 would include). Unconfirmed by any second source; not drawn. Look for a 1941 B&M employee timetable or Milford Cabinet / Nashua Telegraph "last passenger" stories.
Nashua - Wilton end 1936 rests on one secondary source (The Clio); primary floor 1932.
Lowell - Nashua end 1967 and Stony Brook end 1961 are year-level secondary (Karr 2017 via en.wikipedia); primary floor for both is the Feb 1952 Official Guide.
Operator of the 1980-81 MBTA-sponsored trial (Boston and Maine inferred; could be labelled MBTA Commuter Rail).
Opening months: Stony Brook 1848 (the oft-repeated July 1848 unsourced), Wilton RR to Danforth's Corner 1848 (first primary Mar 1850), Peterborough RR 1874.
Who hauled the Concord RR's through trains over Lowell - Nashua 1842-1880s (does not change the track's operator).
The day in late 1880 the B&L took possession under the N&L lease.
Whether the pool (1857-1878) should be its own Rule 4 feature in B&L colour (option (b)) - a maintainer decision.
Exact Wilton Scenic Railroad terminus near Greenfield State Park.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this file is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 2026-10-15 with opstrace.py over OpenStreetMap (maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror), waypoints Lowell (Gallagher Terminal, the MBTA Lowell Line's drawn end), North Chelmsford, Tyngsborough, Nashua junction; 13.6 mi drawn, 100% on OSM rail tagged old_railway_operator=B&M (CSX Middlesex Subdivision to North Chelmsford, then Nashua Subdivision), no straight-line legs, every waypoint within 0.1 km of the line. Documented: 13.4 mi Lowell (25.6) - Nashua Union Station (39.0) from J. Fowler, Southern New England Railroads table 18; 14.5 mi end to end (Upham 1850, N&L to its own Nashua limits); "15 miles" (Pathfinder 1850). Traced length is 1.3% over Fowler's figure. Ends: Lowell is drawn from the B&L's Lowell terminal area (Gallagher Terminal, beside the site of the old Middlesex Street / Lowell Union Station, closed 1959) - the exact 1838 N&L-B&L junction point is not pinned. Nashua is drawn to the junction of the Hillsboro Branch (former Wilton RR) with the main line, taken as the Nashua Union Station site (OSM node at 42.7607 N, 71.4486 W); the N&L's own track on to Nashua City station is drawn with the Wilton features. Alignment era: drawn on the surviving (CSX/Pan Am freight) alignment for every era. Built double track 1848 and later singled under the B&M on the same alignment (en.wikipedia); no relocation is documented. ERA CAVEAT: from 8 Oct to 23 Dec 1838 the line ended at a temporary station south of the Nashua River, short of the drawn Nashua end; not split out (weeks only).

segments.note: Nashua and Lowell, self-operated. Opened 8 Oct 1838 to a temporary station south of the Nashua River; first train through 23 Dec 1838 (en.wikipedia citing Karr 2017). First railroad in New Hampshire; double-tracked 1848. Pathfinder 1850: "15 miles ... opened in Oct, 1838 ... 200,000 passengers ... annually". From 12 Sep 1842 the Concord Railroad's trains ran "in connection with the cars of the Nashua and Lowell" (Caledonian 6 Jun 1843), and in 1850 the Concord's superintendent described Lowell - Nashua as "run over by the Upper Roads" (NH Statesman 21 Jun 1850) - through traffic over N&L track; the N&L remained the line's operator. 1856: the first and last Concord - Boston trains went via the N&L (Granite Farmer 30 Aug 1856), on top of the N&L's own locals and Wilton trains; headway is an estimate, not counted from any timetable.
sources: Segment-level: opening from en.wikipedia (Karr 2017) and Pathfinder 1850; operator from Nashua City Station ("Rail Operations 1838-1880") and the Concord RR cards of 1842/1856 and Upham 1850; end of this era from Springfield Weekly Republican 7 Feb 1857.

segments.note: B&L / N&L POOL ERA (1 Feb 1857 - Dec 1878). On Monday 1 Feb 1857 the Boston and Lowell and the Nashua and Lowell put "the united business" under "one management", with George Stark, the N&L's own superintendent, as Manager for both and the B&L's John B. Winslow as operating superintendent (Springfield Weekly Republican 7 Feb 1857); crews worked both roads (Dollar Weekly Mirror 29 Aug 1857). NOT a lease: each corporation kept its line and revenues were pooled about 69% B&L / 31% N&L. Kept in the N&L feature and colour (research report ownership_split option (a)): the combined operation was headed by the N&L's officer; a B&L-coloured split for these years would also be defensible. Conflicts recorded: en.wikipedia "Boston and Lowell Railroad" dates the joint operation "from 1860" (contradicted by the 1857 primary); en.wikipedia "Stony Brook Railroad" puts the decision to end it in 1877 (the separation itself was Dec 1878). headway is an estimate, not counted from any timetable.
sources: Segment-level: pool start from Springfield Weekly Republican 7 Feb 1857 p.8 (primary); joint crews from Dollar Weekly Mirror 29 Aug 1857; end from Springfield Weekly Republican 6 Dec 1878 p.8 ("the recent separation") and en.wikipedia (Boston Evening Transcript 1878); 69/31 split from en.wikipedia; that this line was worked by the pool is inferred from the N&L operating it on both sides of the pool (research report blocks [2], [7], [10], [13]).

segments.note: Second N&L-alone era: the two companies resumed independent operation in early December 1878 (Springfield Weekly Republican 6 Dec 1878; en.wikipedia citing the Boston Evening Transcript) until the Nashua and Lowell was leased to the Boston and Lowell for 100 years at $60,000 a year (agreed by 5 Nov 1880; B&L stockholders ratified by 26 Nov 1880). The day the B&L took possession was not found; the split year is 1880 either way. headway is an estimate, not counted from any timetable.
sources: Segment-level: separation from Springfield Weekly Republican 6 Dec 1878 p.8; lease from Springfield Weekly Republican 5 Nov 1880 p.8 and 26 Nov 1880 p.8 (primary); Nashua City Station gives the N&L "Rail Operations 1838-1880".

segments.note: Boston and Maine, as lessee of the Boston and Lowell from 1 April 1887 (bought the N&L outright 13 Oct 1944 - paper only). Carried the Boston - Concord - White Mountains / Montreal trains. End 1967 is year-level and secondary (en.wikipedia citing Karr: "Passenger service ended in 1967"; last Boston - Concord round trips 1967 per the B&M research report). The primary floor is the Feb 1952 Official Guide (B&M Tables 1 and 2, Boston - Montreal, legible times at Lowell and Nashua Un. Sta.). Freight continues (Guilford/Pan Am, CSX from 2022) - context only, not drawn. headway is an estimate, not counted from any timetable.
sources: Segment-level: start from en.wikipedia "Boston and Lowell Railroad" ("April 1, 1887"); end from en.wikipedia (Karr 2017), year-level; service confirmed in the Feb 1952 Official Guide Tables 1-2 (Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (schedules eff. 30 Sep 1951), cached at research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt).

segments.note: MBTA-sponsored trial commuter service Boston - Lowell - Nashua - Manchester - Concord, 1980 until suspended in Feb 1981 for low ridership (J. Fowler, New Hampshire Railroads table 10, "s: trial commuter service 1980>1981"; en.wikipedia). OPERATOR INFERRED: the Boston and Maine was the MBTA's contract operator at the time, but neither source names who ran the trains. Commuter rather than intercity service; drawn in this feature because the track and the (inferred) operator are the same. Headway is a rough estimate for a few daily trips; no timetable counted.
sources: Segment-level: dates from J. Fowler, New Hampshire Railroads table 10 and en.wikipedia; operator NOT sourced (inferred).
